;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Terrorism in the United Kingdom]]
**[[Old Bailey]] Justice [[Charles Haddon-Cave]] sentences convicted terrorist [[Umar Haque]], who indoctrinated children he was teaching in [[London]] so that he could use them to commit attacks, to [[life imprisonment in England and Wales|lifetime incarceration]] with parole eligibility only after 25 years. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/crime/umar-haque-jailed-isis-fanatic-who-trained-army-of-children-to-for-terror-attacks-in-london-a3800411.html (''The Evening Standard'')]
*[[Islamophobic incidents in the United Kingdom]]
**Justice Michael Alexander Soole sentences Paul Moore to lifetime incarceration with a minimum imprisonment of 20 years for using his car to attack [[Islam|Muslims]] following a string of terror attacks in 2017 linked to [[Islamic extremism]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/mar/27/man-jailed-life-running-over-muslim-woman-leicester-paul-moore-zaynab-hussein (''The Guardian'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[NATO]] says the [[Afghan Air Force]] dropped its first [[laser-guided bomb]] on a [[Taliban]] compound on March 22. NATO have trained the Afghans in use of the equipment. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/afghan-air-force-drops-laser-guided-bomb-combat-54044424 (ABC)]
*[[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**The government of [[Turkey]] states that eleven [[Kurdistan|Kurdish]] militants have been killed near its [[Syria]]n border, and two soldiers were killed by an explosion in Syria. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2018-03-27/turkey-says-kills-11-kurdish-militants-two-turkish-soldiers-killed (US News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[History of autonomous cars]]
**U.S. [[graphics processing unit]] producer [[Nvidia]] suspends all its tests of self-driving cars. [https://www.theverge.com/2018/3/27/17168606/nvidia-suspends-self-driving-test-uber (The Verge)]
*[[History of the electric vehicle]]s
**The [[United States]] [[National Transportation Safety Board]] (NTSB) launches a probe into a [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]] [[electric vehicles|electric car]] crash and fire in [[California]]. The NTSB says it will investigate issues firefighters had trying to determine how to respond. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-03-27/ntsb-probing-tesla-that-caught-fire-after-crash-in-california (Bloomberg)]
*[[2018 Kemerovo fire]]
**President [[Vladimir Putin]] visits the scene and declares "criminal negligence" responsible for the high death toll. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-43552165 (BBC)]
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2018|Maritime incidents in 2018]]
**Two ships collide in the [[Great Belt]] strait between [[Funen]] and [[Zealand]], near [[Romsø]], [[Denmark]]. One catches fire. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20180327/fire-after-collision-between-ships-in-danish-strait (''The Local'')]
**[[Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency]] (MMEA) expands the search area to 560 square [[nautical mile]]s for nine crewmen missing since March 21 from a capsized [[Dredging|sand dredge]]r off the coast of [[Malaysia]]. MMEA requests for the [[Indonesia]]n [[National Search and Rescue Agency]] to assist in the operation. [http://www.themalaymailonline.com/malaysia/article/search-area-expanded-for-capsized-sand-dredger (''The Malay Mail'')]
*[[2017–18 Volvo Ocean Race]]
**[[Chile]]an search and rescue authorities declare that a crewman who fell overboard from a competitor vessel is lost at sea. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/27/british-yachtsman-missing-sea-falling-overboard-volvo-ocean/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[2018 in aviation]]
**The [[South Korea]]n [[Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board]] issues its final report on the March 2016 near-collision between a [[China Southern Airlines|China Southern]]  [[Airbus A319]] and a [[Korean Air]] [[Boeing 737 Next Generation##737-800|Boeing 737-800]] on a runway in [[Cheongju]], [[South Korea]]. The Board reports the Airbus crew misunderstood the full meaning of the specific ground control runway instruction. [http://avherald.com/h?article=495ba02e&opt=0 (''The Aviation Herald'')]

;International relations
*[[Kim Jong-un and Xi Jinping's meeting]]
**[[North Korea]]'s [[List of leaders of North Korea|supreme leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]] meets with [[China]]'s [[paramount leader]] [[Xi Jinping]] in [[Beijing]], on what is his first known [[List of international trips made by Kim Jong-un|travel]] outside North Korea since assuming office in 2011. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles-china/north-korean-leader-was-in-delegation-visiting-beijing-source-idUSKBN1H305W?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Reactions to the poisoning of Sergei and Yulia Skripal]]
**[[NATO]] and the government of [[Australia]] expel [[Russia]]n diplomats. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/australasia/russia-latest-australia-expels-diplomats-spy-poisoning-sergei-skripal-malclum-turnbull-julie-bishop-a8275221.html (''The Independent'')], [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/mar/27/russia-to-respond-harshly-to-us-expulsion-of-diplomats (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Netherlands–Turkey relations]]
**The government of the [[Netherlands]] recalls a diplomat from [[Turkey]] after local newspapers accused him of spying. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/archives/2018/03/dutch-diplomat-recalled-from-turkey-after-spying-allegations-in-local-press/ (Dutch News)]

;Law and crime
*Aftermath of the [[Manchester Arena bombing]]
**A [[United Kingdom]] panel, chaired by the former [[Civil Service (United Kingdom)#Head of the Home Civil Service|head of the Home civil service]], Lord [[Bob Kerslake]], issues a report which concludes that [[Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service|firefighters]] were prevented from attending the scene of the bombing for two hours. The report makes more than 50 recommendations. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-manchester-43548173 (BBC)]
*[[Censorship in Spain]]
**A [[Madrid]] court issues an order shutting down a website that uses extracts from ''[[Don Quixote]]'' to recreate the book ''Farina''. ''Farina'', an investigation of [[drug trafficking]], is the subject of a [[freedom of speech]] debate after a court halted sales ahead of a [[libel]] case. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/books/don-quixote-helps-spanish-booksellers-in-free-speech-battle/2018/03/27/5b12642e-31b2-11e8-b6bd-0084a1666987_story.html?utm_term=.761f8e29a3ce (AP via ''The Washington Post'')], [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2018/03/17/publisher-beats-spanish-court-gag-recreating-banned-mafia-book/ (''The Telegraph'')]
*[[Crime in the United States]]
**The [[FBI]] arrests [[Everett, Washington]], 43-year-old Thanh Cong Phan on suspicion of charges of illegally shipping explosive materials by sending 12 package bombs to the [[CIA]] as well as multiple military and government facilities in the [[Washington, D.C.]] area. Those devices did not explode. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/washington-dc-suspicious-packages-wrote-letters-military-thanh-cong-phan-2018-03-27/ (CBS News)]
*[[Kent County, Michigan]] special prosecutor Bill Forsyth charges William Strampel, the former dean of the [[Michigan State University College of Osteopathic Medicine]], in the [[United States District Court for the Western District of Michigan]] in [[East Lansing, Michigan]], with misconduct in office, fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct, and two counts of willful neglect of duty in connection with the [[Larry Nassar]] [[USA Gymnastics sex abuse scandal|scandal]]. [https://www.freep.com/story/news/2018/03/27/william-strampel-msu-sexual-assault-larry-nassar/460504002/ (''Detroit Free Press'')]
*[[Law enforcement in the Netherlands]]
**A [[Netherlands|Dutch]] court rules police are liable for a [[mass shooting]] at a shopping centre that killed six and wounded sixteen because the gunman should not have been issued a firearms licence. [https://news.sky.com/story/dutch-police-liable-for-mass-shooting-at-mall-11305979 (Sky News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Egyptian presidential election, 2018]]
**Voting enters the second day. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-election/amid-slow-voting-egypts-sisi-cruises-toward-victory-idUSKBN1H30KW (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Led overall by researchers at [[Aix-Marseille University|Aix-Marseille Université]] in [[France]] using [[NASA]]'s ''[[Kepler (spacecraft)|Kepler Space Telescope]]'', ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature Astronomy]]'' publishes observations of what may be a new [[exoplanet]] named [[K2-229b]], whose attributes may resemble [[Mercury (planet)|the planet of Mercury]] (hot, metallic, and dense). [https://www.healththoroughfare.com/science/nasa-kepler-space-telescope-found-an-exoplanet-similar-to-mercury/6522 (Health Thoroughfare)], [https://phys.org/news/2018-03-newly-discovered-planet-hot-metallic-dense.html (Phys)], [http://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-018-0420-5 (''Nature Astronomy'')]
